subtitle: An independent review of how the website performs for a first-time, full-fee patient — what it does well, and where attention is lost before a booking is made.
summary: The practice has the asset most sites in this review set are missing: a named physician. “by Dr. Sherry Wehner, MD” sits inside the logo on every page, and her photograph appears on the homepage. For a medical aesthetics practice that is the single most valuable trust signal available — the question that decides an injectables booking, answered before it is asked. On a phone there is also a clear green “Schedule Your Free Consultation” button.

Two mechanical problems are getting in the way. The hero is an embedded image rather than a designed section — the zoom, expand and “more options” controls of the embedding widget are visible in its corner, and the words “Wellness - Focused Aesthetics” are pixels inside that picture rather than live text, so search engines and screen readers cannot read them. And directly beneath the mobile booking button, a line of text runs off both edges of the screen: what should read “Schedule your free consultation - (210) 688-4850” appears as “ULTATION - (210) 688-485”, with the practice's telephone number clipped at both ends.

Evidence limitation: this review covers the homepage on desktop and mobile plus publicly visible information. Treatment-page depth and technical performance were not assessed, so the score is normalised across the six categories that were. Nothing here uses private analytics, and no traffic or revenue figures have been estimated.
scoreNote: Normalised across six assessed categories (90 points available). The trust score is held up by Dr. Wehner being named and pictured. Most of what is lost is mechanical — a hero that is a picture of words, and a telephone number that does not fit on the screen.

scorecard.finding: A generic wellness line, set as an image, with no location named.
Dr. Sherry Wehner MD named and pictured; no reviews shown.
A clear mobile booking button; nothing at all on the desktop first screen.
The desktop opening screen offers no action of any kind.
A line of text overflows both edges, clipping the telephone number.
San Antonio does not appear on the first screen.

strengthsLead: One of these is worth more than everything else on this page, and it is already in place.

strengths.title: The physician is named in the logo itself.
strengths.body: “by Dr. Sherry Wehner, MD” travels on every page rather than sitting on an About page nobody reaches. For injectables the decision is about a person, and this answers who — permanently, everywhere. Very few practices do this.

strengths.title: Her photograph is on the homepage.
strengths.body: A real portrait, not a stock clinician. A patient can see who they would be trusting before they commit to anything, which does more to settle nerves than any amount of description.

strengths.title: “Schedule Your Free Consultation” asks plainly.
strengths.body: The mobile button says exactly what happens next and removes the cost objection in the same four words. Free consultation is the right offer for a first-time aesthetic patient and it is stated without hedging.

strengths.title: “Medical Aesthetics and Total Wellness Center”.
strengths.body: The strapline in the logo does real work — it sets the practice apart from the beauty-salon end of the market and signals the wider wellness offering at the same time.

captionDesktop: Desktop, 1366×768. The hero is an embedded image with the widget's zoom and expand controls visible in its lower corner. No booking button, telephone number or location appears.
captionMobile: Mobile, 390×844. Beneath the booking button, a line of text runs off both edges — the telephone number is clipped at each end.

findings.heading: The telephone number is cut off at both ends on a phone.
findings.evidence: At 390×844, directly below the green booking button, a line renders as “ULTATION - (210) 688-485” — running past both the left and right edges of the screen. The opening words and the final digit are outside the viewport.
findings.why: A patient who wants to telephone cannot read the number. Worse, a partially visible number invites them to dial what they can see, and a wrong number is a lost patient who believes they tried. It also makes an otherwise professional page look broken at precisely the moment trust is being formed.
findings.recommended: Let that line wrap instead of overflowing, and make the number a tap-to-call link so it dials rather than has to be read and copied.

findings.heading: The headline is a picture of words, not words.
findings.evidence: “Wellness - Focused Aesthetics” and “Complete Revitalization from the Inside Out” sit inside an embedded image. The embedding widget's own controls — zoom, expand and a “more options” button — are visible in the lower corner of it on both desktop and mobile.
findings.why: Text inside an image cannot be read by search engines, cannot be read aloud by a screen reader, and cannot be selected or resized by a visitor who needs larger type. The most prominent words on the homepage are invisible to the systems that decide whether the practice is found at all — and the visible widget controls make the section look like a document that has been dropped onto the page rather than part of it.
findings.recommended: Rebuild the hero as ordinary text over a background image. Same design, but the words become real, and the widget controls disappear.

findings.heading: The desktop first screen offers nothing to do.
findings.evidence: At 1366×768 the opening screen carries the logo on a green band, a hamburger button, and the embedded hero image. There is no booking button, no telephone number, no address and no navigation bar — every menu item is behind the hamburger.
findings.why: Hiding the whole menu behind a button is normal on a phone and costly on a desktop, where there is room to show it. Combined with no visible way to book or call, a desktop visitor reaching this page has no offered next step at all — the mobile version is markedly better served than the desktop one.
findings.recommended: Show the navigation across the desktop header, and add the booking button and telephone number beside it. The mobile page already proves the practice knows what to ask for.

findings.heading: San Antonio does not appear on the first screen.
findings.evidence: Neither the desktop nor the mobile opening screen names a town, an address or a region. The headline is “Wellness - Focused Aesthetics”.
findings.why: Proximity is the first filter an aesthetic patient applies, and the headline currently spends its space on a sentiment that would suit any practice in the country. A visitor cannot tell whether this is ten minutes away or in another state.
findings.recommended: Put “San Antonio” into the headline alongside the treatments — and when the hero becomes real text, that line will also be readable by search engines for the first time.

psychology.plain: People expect a site to behave like the others they use.
psychology.site: A desktop page with no visible navigation, and a hero showing an embedded widget's controls, are both outside what visitors expect.

psychology.plain: Important actions should be big and easy to thumb.
psychology.site: The mobile booking button is a good, generous target. On desktop there is nothing to aim at.

psychology.plain: Reassurance has to sit where the doubt is.
psychology.site: Dr. Wehner's photograph is on the page but below the booking button rather than beside it.
The strongest category here. A named physician carried in the logo on every page is rare and valuable.
Clear on mobile — schedule a free consultation. Absent entirely on desktop.

psychology.plain: Sensible pre-selections that serve the patient.
psychology.site: Offering the consultation free, and saying so on the button, removes the objection before it is raised.

psychology.plain: Balanced, realistic communication is trusted more than perfection.
psychology.site: There is very little overclaiming here. “Complete Revitalization from the Inside Out” is the vaguest line, and the named physician more than balances it.

roadmap.actions: Fix the overflowing line so the telephone number is fully visible, and make it tap-to-call. Show the navigation and a booking button on the desktop header. Add San Antonio to the first screen.

Rebuild the hero as real text over a background image so the headline becomes readable to search engines. Move Dr. Wehner's photograph and credential up beside the booking button. Add a rating with its review count.

Build authority content under Dr. Wehner's name — it is the strongest asset the practice has. Treatment-page depth with candidacy and downtime notes. Begin measuring enquiry-to-booking so the calculator figures above become yours.

limitations: This review assessed the homepage at 1366×768 and at 390 pixels wide, together with publicly visible information. Treatment-page depth and technical performance were not assessed and are excluded from the score rather than estimated; the total is normalised across the six categories reviewed (90 points available). The overflowing line described above was measured on what is visible without horizontal scrolling.
